title: The Evolution of Trust
summary: A playable essay where repeated trust decisions, strategy comparison, and simulation outcomes progressively carry the argument about cooperation.

interaction_model.trigger: make repeated trust/cheat decisions and advance through strategy experiments
interaction_model.response: Immediate payoffs and later simulations turn the user's earlier decisions into evidence for the next explanatory step.

transfer_constraints: Let interaction generate evidence that the narrative later interprets; do not bolt a mini-game beside unrelated prose.
Keep the model rules simple enough that users can form and revise expectations through play.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse the playable-model structure without copying characters, drawings, text, payoff tables, or narrative voice.
failure_modes: Do not turn every explanation into a game when the model has no meaningful decision.
Do not hide the rules so completely that outcomes feel arbitrary.

title: Parable of the Polygons
summary: A direct-manipulation simulation where users move agents, alter local preference rules, and observe emergent segregation at the system level.

interaction_model.trigger: drag unhappy polygons or change the local bias rule
interaction_model.response: Agent satisfaction and the global pattern update from the same rule set, exposing how small local preferences accumulate.

transfer_constraints: Expose local rules and global consequences at the same time so users can connect individual state to emergent pattern.
Include reset/sandbox states that let users test counterfactual rules rather than follow one scripted path.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse the direct-manipulation/emergence mechanism without copying characters, story text, illustration style, or exact simulation parameters.
failure_modes: Do not imply a social model predicts real populations without its stated assumptions.
Do not animate agents independently of the same model used for satisfaction/output.

title: Seeing Theory — Basic Probability
summary: An interactive probability lesson where users reshape distributions and immediately observe sampling, expectation, variance, and related representations from one shared model.

interaction_model.trigger: drag probability values, sample, or alter distribution parameters
interaction_model.response: Samples and derived statistical quantities update from the manipulated distribution, preserving one source of truth across representations.

transfer_constraints: Keep probability parameters, simulated samples, and derived summaries synchronized rather than calculating each view independently.
Make the manipulated quantity visually explicit before showing derived statistics.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse the linked model/representation structure without copying Seeing Theory's artwork, prose, charts, or exercises.
failure_modes: Do not fabricate samples that are disconnected from the displayed distribution.
Do not infer statistical validity outside the model assumptions.

tool_choices.reason: Seeing Theory project documentation states that its interactive visualizations were built with D3.js.

title: Image Kernels — Explained Visually
summary: A convolution explainer that links source pixels, a local 3×3 operation, kernel values, and the transformed output under hover and editable matrices.

interaction_model.trigger: hover a pixel, select/edit a kernel, or supply an image/video source
interaction_model.response: The local neighborhood, numerical operation, kernel, and transformed output stay linked to the same selected location and parameters.

transfer_constraints: Use one selection/hover state to connect the input neighborhood, calculation, and output result.
Let users move from presets to custom parameters only after the local operation is legible.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse the linked-computation mechanism without copying Setosa illustrations, examples, wording, or image assets.
failure_modes: Do not show a transformed output without exposing which local values generated it.
Do not imply every image operation is a linear convolution.

title: Markov Chains — Explained Visually
summary: A state-transition explainer where an editable transition matrix, animated states, speed control, validation, and sandbox behavior remain synchronized.

interaction_model.trigger: edit transition probabilities, choose examples/random models, or change playback speed
interaction_model.response: The state graph/animation follows the same transition matrix and invalid inputs receive immediate feedback before simulation.

transfer_constraints: Keep symbolic parameters and animated state transitions derived from one model.
Validate editable models close to the control that created the invalid state rather than silently normalizing them.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse the editable-state-model pattern without copying Setosa layouts, prose, examples, or styling.
failure_modes: Do not animate transitions that are not present in the matrix.
Do not hide invalid probability structure behind automatic correction without explanation.

title: 100,000 Stars
summary: A navigable 3D stellar neighborhood where continuous zoom changes the level of named/contextual information while preserving spatial orientation.

interaction_model.trigger: zoom, orbit, and move through the stellar neighborhood
interaction_model.response: Spatial scale changes continuously while labels/context emerge at useful levels instead of merely enlarging pixels.

transfer_constraints: Tie added detail to meaningful scale thresholds while preserving orientation across zoom levels.
Keep the global neighborhood understandable even as local named objects become available.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse semantic zoom and spatial navigation without copying star-rendering assets, tour narration, or Google visual identity.
failure_modes: Do not add labels at every scale until the space becomes unreadable.
Do not treat ordinary camera zoom as semantic zoom unless information granularity changes.

title: earth :: global wind, weather and ocean conditions
summary: A rotatable global field visualization that combines animated vector flow with scalar overlays, time/altitude controls, data modes, and projection changes in one spatial model.

interaction_model.trigger: rotate/zoom the globe, change time/height, switch overlays or projection
interaction_model.response: Vector flow and scalar context re-render over one geographic frame while the chosen physical/data dimension changes.

transfer_constraints: Keep vector flow, scalar overlay, spatial frame, and time/height controls visibly coordinated.
Use mode changes to swap physical meaning without fragmenting each data layer into a separate chart.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse the integrated field-navigation structure without copying map styling, data assets, or branding; preserve units/source semantics in any scientific adaptation.
failure_modes: Do not present particle motion as measured trajectories when it is a field visualization.
Do not mix overlays with incompatible physical meaning or units without clear labeling.

title: Bruno Simon — 3D portfolio
summary: A portfolio navigated by driving a vehicle through one persistent 3D world, with keyboard/touch/mouse/gamepad input plus map, reset, respawn, and alternate access affordances.

interaction_model.trigger: steer the vehicle with keyboard, touch, mouse, or gamepad
interaction_model.response: Movement through the world becomes navigation among portfolio objects while map/reset/respawn controls preserve recoverability.

transfer_constraints: If navigation becomes embodied, provide explicit control mapping, recovery, and a non-spatial fallback path.
Keep the camera/world relationship stable enough that users learn the space rather than fighting it.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse the world-as-interface and recoverability principles without copying Bruno Simon's car, world, projects, models, or sound design.
failure_modes: Do not force a game-like world on information that needs fast direct lookup.
Do not remove conventional access entirely when spatial control may be inaccessible or slow.

tool_choices.reason: The portfolio documentation identifies Three.js as the 3D rendering foundation.
The portfolio documentation identifies Rapier for physics.

title: Chrome Music Lab — Kandinsky
summary: A drawing interface where marks simultaneously become visible composition and sound-producing input, coupling gesture and audio in one creative surface.

interaction_model.trigger: draw lines and shapes on the canvas
interaction_model.response: The same gesture creates visible form and corresponding sound behavior, so drawing and musical input are one action.

transfer_constraints: Map input dimensions to visual and sonic behavior coherently so users can learn the cross-modal instrument through action.
Keep latency low enough that gesture and feedback are perceived as one event.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse the coupled gesture-to-sound principle without copying Kandinsky's exact mappings, art direction, sounds, or Google branding.
failure_modes: Do not add sound as an unrelated after-effect to a visual action.
Do not create mappings so arbitrary that repeated gestures fail to build user expectation.

title: Patatap
summary: A minimal browser instrument mapping discrete keyboard/touch input to tightly synchronized animation and sound responses with almost no interface chrome.

interaction_model.trigger: press mapped keys or use touch input
interaction_model.response: Each discrete action immediately launches a coordinated visual and sonic response, allowing rhythmic composition through repeated input.

transfer_constraints: Keep the input vocabulary simple and feedback immediate enough that the interface behaves like an instrument.
Let repeated discrete mappings combine into emergent rhythm rather than wrapping them in heavy control chrome.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse the immediate audiovisual mapping principle without copying Patatap's animations, sounds, key mappings, or branding.
failure_modes: Do not introduce perceptible latency between input and multimodal feedback.
Do not overload the surface with explanatory UI that competes with playing.

title: Pulse Room
summary: A biometric installation where a participant's heartbeat appears immediately in one bulb, then enters a finite spatial queue of previous participants' pulse recordings.

interaction_model.response: The nearest bulb flashes the current pulse, then the recording joins a spatial queue that shifts prior participants' pulses through the room.

transfer_constraints: Separate immediate personal feedback from the persistent/shared-history representation while deriving both from the same sensed event.
Use finite memory/queue behavior to make previous participation visibly present rather than storing history invisibly.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse the sensor→immediate feedback→collective history mechanism without copying the bulb installation, physical layout, or artwork identity.
failure_modes: Do not treat sensitive biometric data casually in contexts where privacy/consent are relevant.
Do not fake individual histories if real participation is the stated meaning.

title: Rain Room
summary: An environmental installation where tracked human presence subtracts rainfall locally, creating a moving dry volume around visitors while the surrounding field continues.

interaction_model.trigger: walk through the tracked rain field
interaction_model.response: Presence tracking suppresses rainfall only in the participant's local volume while the rest of the environmental field remains active.

transfer_constraints: Consider interaction as subtraction/carving from a continuous field rather than adding a cursor, panel, or object.
Keep the environmental baseline visible so the user's negative-space effect can be perceived.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse the presence-mediated field principle without copying the Rain Room installation, rain hardware, layout, or artwork identity.
failure_modes: Do not imply perfect tracking or safety behavior outside documented conditions.
Do not reduce the mechanism to a decorative spotlight following the user.

title: teamLab Borderless
summary: A spatial exhibition where artworks migrate across rooms and context follows the visitor, so content is not owned by one fixed wall, screen, or container.

interaction_model.trigger: move through the museum and encounter migrating works
interaction_model.response: Artworks cross room boundaries while location-relative guidance and participation maintain context around the visitor rather than around a fixed container.

transfer_constraints: Allow content identity to persist when it moves between containers or contexts.
Attach orientation/help to current location or nearby content when fixed labels would contradict the spatial model.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse the boundaryless-content/context principle without copying teamLab artworks, environments, interaction assets, or museum layout.
failure_modes: Do not remove all labels/context unless an alternate orientation mechanism exists.
Do not call ordinary carousel/page transitions 'boundaryless' when content is still container-owned.

title: UVA — Momentum
summary: A long gallery becomes a spatial instrument of moving elements, evolving light and sound, with each visitor experiencing the temporal work through their own pace and path.

interaction_model.trigger: walk through the evolving installation at an individual pace
interaction_model.response: Position along the path determines which phase, light condition, sound, shadow, and kinetic relation the visitor encounters.

transfer_constraints: Compose temporal change across a path so user pace selects a slice of one system rather than triggering unrelated scenes.
Use anticipation, occlusion, sound, and partial visibility to connect adjacent spatial moments.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse the path-paced choreography principle without copying UVA's kinetic elements, light program, sounds, or Barbican installation geometry.
failure_modes: Do not require synchronized user timing when the mechanism depends on self-paced traversal.
Do not turn every step into a discrete trigger if continuous spatial progression is the point.

title: Ryoji Ikeda — data-verse 3
summary: A large-scale audiovisual installation that treats scientific and computational data as an immersive compositional field of density, precision, rhythm, layering, and scale.

interaction_model.trigger: occupy and watch the environment-scale audiovisual composition
interaction_model.response: Data imagery and sound operate as one timed spatial field whose density and scale dominate the viewer's attention rather than reading as separate charts.

transfer_constraints: Use data density, layering, rhythm, and spatial scale as deliberate representational variables rather than dashboard decoration.
Preserve data/source semantics whenever an adaptation makes factual scientific claims.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse data-as-environment/display principles without copying Ikeda's visual language, datasets, audio, sequences, or installation design.
failure_modes: Do not call arbitrary code-like texture 'data visualization' without real data semantics.
Do not sacrifice necessary legibility when the task requires analytical reading rather than immersive perception.

title: Random International — Future Self
summary: A tracked full-body image is aggressively reduced to sparse points of light and slightly delayed, yet movement and bodily identity remain recognizable.

interaction_model.trigger: move in front of the tracked light installation
interaction_model.response: 3D body motion is translated into a sparse, slightly delayed LED representation that preserves recognizable posture/movement despite information reduction.

transfer_constraints: Reduce visual information while preserving the motion/identity cues necessary for self-recognition.
Treat controlled latency as a perceptual parameter only when it supports the relationship between body and representation.
fidelity_constraints: Reuse the abstraction/embodiment mechanism without copying the installation geometry, LED design, calibration, or artwork identity.
failure_modes: Do not assume low resolution automatically preserves identity; select cues deliberately.
Do not present tracking latency as intentional unless it is actually controlled and perceptually useful.
